title: perf(app-shell,react): a console open reads the current app's objects, not the whole object registry (objectui#12811)
body:
Part of #12811
Clause-②: yes

The object list open path (the card's measured route, /apps/crm_enterprise/crm_account) no longer requests the whole object registry. One half of the card stays open: record routes and record overlays still read the whole registry, because a record's related lists come from every object that points at its object, in any package. On HotCRM, crm_case (app.objectstack.hotcrm.service) points at crm_account. That half needs a decision (a reverse-relation door, or keep as is), recorded on the card.

## What changed

**The scoped read** (`@object-ui/react`, `MetadataProvider`). A new optional member, `MetadataContextValue.readObjectScope({ packageId, names })`:
- reads `GET /api/v1/meta/object?package=ID` with the package id the app's served item carries (ADR-0048; `@objectstack/client`'s `meta.getItems(type, { packageId })` sends it);
- reads each named object the package does not hold by name, through the provider's existing `getItem`;
- uses the same ingestion as the whole list (`normalizeSchemaReferenceKeys`, then `composeObjects`), so a scoped definition equals the same object from `objects`;
- returns `objects`, `served` (the definitions as served, before views are merged), `missing` and `settled`;
- with no package id, returns the whole registry.

Scope entries are dropped and refetched only with the `object` type (`invalidate`, `refresh`, an organization or preview-mode switch); there is no timestamp. When the whole registry is already loaded (after Studio, say), a scope is cut from it and nothing is requested. `useMetadata().objects` is unchanged: it is the whole registry wherever it is read.

**Which route reads what** (`console/appObjectScope.ts`). These routes read the app's scope: the app root, an object's list, and a list view, with no record overlay in the URL and an app item that carries a package id. They read the package's objects, plus by name:
- the route's own object;
- the objects its lookup fields point at;
- the objects the app's navigation entries name in `requiresObject`;
- while the command palette is open, the navigation's objects.

The splash and the route skeleton wait for the package list and the route's own object. The other names are asked in parallel and are not waited on: a lookup cell draws its value without a link until its target lands.

Everything else reads the whole registry, as before:
- record routes and record overlays;
- a list whose views open records in an in-page overlay (modal, split, popover);
- an app whose package holds no objects of its own (Setup and Account on HotCRM);
- an app item without a package id (none on HotCRM);
- every route outside an app.

**The open path's readers, and what each reads now:**
- `AppContent`: the scope for the route element, `ConsoleLayout`, `CommandPalette` and `useTrackRouteAsRecent`. It no longer destructures `objects`.
- `useActionModal` (mounted from `ConsoleShell`): reads `objects` only while an object's form modal is open, and the open waits for `ensureType('object')`. The form's subforms are derived from every object.
- `useNavMemberGates`: inside an app with a package, while nothing has loaded the whole registry, answers from the scope. It asks for nothing itself.
- `useServedViewItems` (AppHeader and ObjectView view-tab labels) and `useObjectPresence` (the bell's activity feed): read the scope until something loads the whole registry. These two were found live; main hid them because the whole list was already in flight.
- `ConsoleShell`: starts the app's scope as soon as the app list names the app. `AppContent` mounts only after the session's permission read, while the whole list used to start at the console root beside it.

`openPathObjectReaders-12811.test.ts` finds every reader of `objects` or `getItemsByType('object')` in the packages and the console, and fails on one it does not classify (scope, action time, or off the open path).

## Requests, measured

HotCRM `objectstack dev --fresh`, behind a proxy adding 25 ms on each leg (a 50 ms round trip), production builds served by `vite preview`, Chromium via Playwright: one warm open, then three measured opens per side of `/apps/crm_enterprise/crm_account`. Times are milliseconds from navigation start.

| | main e43a162 | this branch e7a2e8a |
|---|---|---|
| splash on screen | 783-1660, 900-1654, 711-1513 (877, 754, 802 ms) | 731-1471, 852-1632, 808-1589 (740, 780, 781 ms) |
| meta/object (whole) | 96 objects, 858893 B, 869-1078 | not requested |
| meta/object?package=app.objectstack.hotcrm | none | 15 objects, 316198 B, 1002-1159 |
| by name: sys_approval_request, sys_organization, sys_user, sys_business_unit | none | 1 each, 7957-24199 B, 1170-1329 |
| by name: sys_activity (bell) | none | 1, 8074 B, 1206-1433 |
| meta/object/crm_account (the adapter's own read, both sides) | 49786 B, after paint | 49786 B, after paint |
| object bytes, total | 908679 B in 2 calls | 430281 B in 7 calls |
| API calls in the open | 32 | 37 |

On the Setup app (`/apps/setup`, a package with no objects of its own): main 35 calls, splash 855 ms; branch 36 calls (one empty `?package=` answer, then the whole list), splash 858 ms.

On this local backend the whole list costs about 200 ms, so the splash does not move. The card measured it at 5.7 s on staging, which this read no longer makes on the object-list open.

## Controls, live

- Record page `/apps/crm_enterprise/crm_account/record/01T4qqNXvOOOINtK`: the Account Owner lookup (`sys_user`, outside the package) renders as Dev Admin, with 16 related lists. Same on main and on the branch.
- Metadata admin `/apps/crm_enterprise/metadata/object`: still requests the whole `meta/object` when it mounts and lists the same rows on both sides.
- `/apps/crm_enterprise/crm_case` (an object outside the app's package): asked by name, renders its list, no not-found state.

## Deviations

- Files beyond the claim's list: `packages/react/src/context/AppShellContext.tsx` (the context type), the new `console/appObjectScope.ts`, `ConsoleShell.tsx`, `useServedViewItems.ts`, `useObjectPresence.ts`. Existing pins: `ConnectedShell.sessionGate.test.tsx` (its third boot request was the whole list) and a comment in `MetadataProvider.requestBudget.test.tsx`.
- One new optional member on `MetadataContextValue`.
- Values that now resolve differently: an object form modal waits for the object list the first time; `useObjectPresence` and the capability gate answer from the app scope inside an app with a package; the bell's cross-app roster no longer asks other apps' `requiresObject` objects by name.
- Record surfaces and apps without objects of their own keep the whole registry, for the measured reasons above.

## Screenshots (light, evidence branch, not merged here)

- The object list route after the change: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/blob/ded02e9cb491ea70ec00e7ba5820e9a34deb9a51/docs/design/findings/12811/object-list-after-12811.png?raw=true
- A record page whose Account Owner lookup points at sys_user, outside the app's package: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/blob/ded02e9cb491ea70ec00e7ba5820e9a34deb9a51/docs/design/findings/12811/record-cross-package-lookup-12811.png?raw=true

## Tests, pinned to e7a2e8a

- `MetadataProvider.objectScope-12811`:
  - asks `?package=`, never the bare list;
  - asks a name outside the package after the list, and is not settled until it answers;
  - a scoped definition equals the whole list's;
  - an unanswered name is `missing`;
  - CONTROL: `objects` is the whole registry, and so is a scope with no package;
  - with the whole registry loaded, a scope requests nothing;
  - `invalidate` and `refresh` drop and refetch it.
- `AppContent.objectScope-12811` (real provider, recorded client):
  - the open asks the package list and only the by-name objects it reads;
  - CONTROL: an app item with no package id, or a package with no objects of its own, asks the whole registry;
  - CONTROL: a record overlay reads the whole registry;
  - a route object outside the package holds the splash, then after the first paint the route skeleton, until it lands;
  - lookup targets do not hold the route.
- `appObjectScope-12811`: the console root asks the package list, then the lookup targets; nothing outside an app, on a record overlay, or for an app without a package id.
- `scopedRegistryReaders-12811`: `useServedViewItems` and `useObjectPresence` read the scope inside an app; CONTROLs outside an app and once the whole registry loads.
- `openPathObjectReaders-12811`: the census, in both directions.
- Ablation, one per new pin, each mutation confirmed on disk and each restore confirmed by an empty `git diff HEAD`: whole-registry forced (3 red), scope readiness dropped (2 red), a new `objects` reader in AppHeader (census red), `objects` made partial (2 red), `useServedViewItems` reverted (1 red), no-own-objects rule deleted (1 red), gate waiting for lookups (1 red).
- app-shell in 8 shards (`pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/ --shard=K/8`; the whole suite exceeds the container's foreground cap): every shard exit 0, 1539 files (1538 passed, 1 skipped), 14516 tests passed, 9 skipped.
- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/` in 2 shards (it also exceeds the cap): both exit 0, 223 files, 2304 tests. `packages/react`: 113 files, 1426 tests.
- `type-check` and `build` for `@object-ui/react` and `@object-ui/app-shell`: 0. Console build: 0.
- `check:eager-closure` 0, `check:spec-symbols` 0, `check:i18n-keys` 0, `check:i18n-drift` 0, `check:new-line-citations` 0, `check:test-path-roots` 0, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` 0.
- eslint on the touched files: 0 errors; the added warnings are `no-explicit-any`, in the files' existing idiom.

## Acceptance notes

- Not filed, observed on both sides: the adapter fetches the route object by name for its own schema cache after the first paint, and `meta/view` is asked three more times after the first paint.
- HotCRM declares no `inlineEdit` field, so a scope's `attachInlineSubforms` sees the same children as the whole list there. The record form, which shows subforms, reads the whole registry everywhere.
